$comment: Rules engine operator specification, spec_version 1.0 (docs/04 §4.1, decision D-29). Implemented identically by fess_pos_engine (Dart) and @fess-pos/engine (TS); every operator has fixtures in schema/fixtures/rules/<fixture>.json. Adding an operator is a minor spec_version bump.

syntax.expression: A JSON literal (null, boolean, finite number, string), an array of expressions (each element evaluated), or an operator object with exactly one key — the operator name — whose value is the argument list. A non-array value is sugar for a one-element list (e.g. {"var": "answers.x"}, {"!": {"var": "answers.y"}}). Zero-argument operators take [] (e.g. {"today": []}). There is no literal-object syntax: every object is an operator.
syntax.strict_typing: No implicit coercion anywhere. == compares type and value (1 == "1" is false). Operators that need a type raise RULE_TYPE_ERROR when given another (non-null) type.
syntax.null_safety: var on a missing path yields null (or its default). Ordering comparisons involving null are false. Logical operators treat null as false. Arithmetic propagates null except + / min / max, which skip nulls. empty treats null, "" and [] as empty.
syntax.short_circuit: and, or and if evaluate arguments left to right and stop as soon as the result is known; errors in unevaluated arguments are not raised. Both engines must short-circuit identically.
syntax.scopes: Inside the predicate of some/all/none/count the data is the outer data plus current (the element) and current_index (its index); nested iterations shadow them. Inside options_filter the option being tested is bound as option ({value, label, meta}). Inside repeatable-group children item and index are bound. list_page / job_list / stat_tile filters bind the record under its source name (job, inspection, record).
syntax.determinism: No I/O and no wall clock. today is taken from the evaluation environment (frozen to the inspection start date and recorded in context_snapshot.today). Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles in both engines; results must be finite (RULE_NUMERIC_OVERFLOW otherwise).

limits.counting: Every operator object, literal and literal array is one node (literal-only arguments included). An operator's argument list is not itself a node, so {"!": true} and {"!": [true]} are both 2 nodes with depth 2. Depth: a bare literal is 1; each enclosing operator or literal array adds 1.

error_codes.RULE_MALFORMED: Not a valid expression: non-JSON value, non-finite number, or an object without exactly one key.
error_codes.RULE_UNKNOWN_OPERATOR: Operator name not in this list.
error_codes.RULE_INVALID_ARGUMENT: A literal-only argument is not a literal of the required kind (var path, date unit, round decimals, option_meta keys, matches pattern).
error_codes.RULE_TYPE_ERROR: An argument has the wrong (non-null) type at evaluation time.
error_codes.RULE_UNSAFE_REGEX: matches pattern uses a construct outside the RE2-safe subset.
error_codes.RULE_INVALID_DATE: A date argument is not an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD, or an ISO datetime with offset whose date part is used), or a result falls outside years 0000–9999.
error_codes.RULE_INVALID_POINT: A geo argument is not {lat, lng} within range.
error_codes.RULE_NO_TODAY: today used without a valid frozen date in the environment.

operators.name: var
operators.semantics: Reads a dotted path from the data ("answers.premises_type", "job.attributes.risk_tier", "items.0.name" — numeric segments index arrays; "" returns the whole data). Only own properties are read. If the value is missing or null, returns the evaluated default when given, else null. The path must be a literal string so dependencies are static.
operators.null_behaviour: missing or null → default or null

operators.name: and
operators.semantics: True when every operand is true. Short-circuits on the first false.

operators.name: or
operators.semantics: True when any operand is true. Short-circuits on the first true.
Logical negation.

operators.name: if
operators.semantics: [c1, v1, c2, v2, …, else?]. Returns the value after the first true condition; otherwise the trailing else value, or null when there is none. Conditions must be boolean.
Strict deep equality: same JSON type and value; arrays element-wise; objects by key set and values (key order irrelevant). Never coerces.
operators.null_behaviour: null == null is true; null == anything else is false

operators.semantics: Negation of ==.
Both numbers (numeric order) or both strings (UTF-16 code-unit order — ISO dates and HH:mm times order correctly). Mixed types raise RULE_TYPE_ERROR.
operators.null_behaviour: false when either side is null

operators.semantics: As <.
operators.null_behaviour: false when either side is null

operators.semantics: As <.
operators.null_behaviour: false when either side is null

operators.semantics: As <.
operators.null_behaviour: false when either side is null

operators.name: between
operators.semantics: low <= x <= high (inclusive both ends), same typing as <.
operators.null_behaviour: false when any argument is null

operators.name: in
operators.semantics: Array haystack: some element == needle (strict). String haystack: needle must be a string and a substring.
operators.null_behaviour: null haystack → false; null needle in a string → false

operators.name: contains
operators.semantics: in with the arguments reversed: {"contains": [answers.services, "delivery"]}.

operators.name: some
operators.semantics: True when the predicate is true for at least one element (current / current_index bound). False for an empty array.

operators.name: all
operators.semantics: True when the predicate is true for every element. False for an empty array (JsonLogic behaviour).

operators.name: none
operators.semantics: True when the predicate is true for no element. True for an empty array.

operators.name: count
operators.semantics: Number of elements, or of elements matching the optional predicate.

operators.name: empty
operators.semantics: True for null, "" and []. Everything else (0, false, {}) is not empty.

operators.name: not_empty
operators.semantics: Negation of empty.

operators.name: length
operators.semantics: String: number of Unicode code points (Dart: runes.length). Array: element count.

operators.name: starts_with
operators.semantics: Case-sensitive prefix test.

operators.name: matches
operators.semantics: Unanchored search with a literal pattern in the RE2-safe subset: compiled with Unicode mode (JS flag u, Dart unicode: true), case-sensitive, '.' excludes newlines. Rejected at check time: backreferences, lookarounds, named/atomic groups, inline flags (only '(?:' is allowed), a repeated group that contains a repeating quantifier or an alternation, more than regex_max_unbounded_quantifiers unbounded quantifiers, repeat counts above regex_max_repeat, patterns longer than regex_max_length. Inputs longer than match_input_max_length raise RULE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

operators.name: lower
operators.semantics: Locale-independent Unicode lower-casing.

operators.name: concat
operators.semantics: Joins strings. Numbers are not converted (avoids cross-language number formatting); use templates for display.
Sum of the non-null terms.
operators.null_behaviour: null terms are skipped; all null → null

operators.semantics: One argument: negation. Two: a − b.
Product.
a ÷ b.
operators.null_behaviour: any null → null; division by zero → null

operators.name: min
operators.semantics: Smallest non-null value.

operators.name: max
operators.semantics: Largest non-null value.

operators.name: round
operators.semantics: Round half away from zero to `decimals` (literal 0–10, default 0): r = floor(|x| × 10^d + 0.5) ÷ 10^d with the sign of x restored; −0 becomes 0. Both engines use exactly this double arithmetic.

operators.name: abs
operators.semantics: Absolute value.

operators.name: today
operators.semantics: The frozen evaluation date (YYYY-MM-DD) from the environment — never the device clock. Raises RULE_NO_TODAY if none was supplied.

operators.name: date_diff
operators.semantics: Whole units from `from` to `to` (negative when `to` is earlier). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD or ISO datetimes with offset (the written date part is used; no time-zone conversion). days: difference of proleptic-Gregorian day numbers. months: (y2−y1)×12 + (m2−m1), minus 1 when d2 < d1 (computed on the ordered pair, sign restored). years: months truncated toward zero ÷ 12.

operators.name: date_add
operators.semantics: Adds an integer amount (|amount| ≤ max_date_add_amount) and returns YYYY-MM-DD. Month and year arithmetic clamps the day to the end of the target month (2024-01-31 + 1 month = 2024-02-29).

operators.name: distance_m
operators.semantics: Haversine great-circle distance in metres with R = 6371008.8 m: h = sin²(Δφ/2) + cos φ1 · cos φ2 · sin²(Δλ/2); d = R · 2 · atan2(√h, √(1−h)); rounded half away from zero to 3 decimals. Points are {lat, lng} in decimal degrees (extra keys ignored).

operators.name: within_m
operators.semantics: distance_m(a, b) <= metres.
operators.null_behaviour: false when any argument is null

operators.name: option_meta
operators.semantics: Reads metadata of the selected option. path is the answer path (e.g. "answers.premises_type" or "item.kind"); its last segment names the field whose options are consulted. Single value → that option's meta[meta_key] (null when absent). Array (multi_select) → array of meta values, one per selected value (null where absent). The engine is given option metadata per field by the resolver (fixtures: env.option_meta).
